Nuh was pious and truthful; Allah sent him to guide his people and warn them of the punishment of the Hereafter, but they disobeyed him and called him a liar. Despite this, he continued to call them to the upright religion, and a few people followed him, while the disbelievers persisted in their transgression. So Allah withheld the rain from them, and Nuh called them to believe so that Allah would lift the punishment from them; they believed and Allah lifted the punishment, but they returned to their disbelief. He kept calling them for nine hundred and fifty years; then Allah commanded him to build the ark and to take with him a pair of every kind; then the flood came and drowned them all.

Ibrahim: he is the Friend of Allah; Allah chose him for His message and favoured him over many of His creation. Ibrahim lived among a people who worshipped the stars, and that did not satisfy him; he sensed by his innate nature that there is a greater God, until Allah guided him and chose him for His message. Ibrahim began calling his people to the oneness of Allah and His worship, but they denied him and tried to burn him, and Allah saved him from their hands. Allah made the prophets from the progeny of Ibrahim: Isma‘il and Ishaq were born to him. Ibrahim built the Ka‘bah together with Isma‘il.

Musa is a messenger whom Allah the Exalted sent to Pharaoh and his people, and supported with two miracles: one of them is the staff that swallowed the serpents; the other was his hand, which he would put into his bosom and it would come out white without any blemish. Musa called to the oneness of Allah, so Pharaoh fought him and gathered the sorcerers against him to plot against him, but he defeated them by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Then Allah commanded him to leave Egypt with those who followed him, and Pharaoh pursued him with a great army; and when his followers thought they would be overtaken, Allah commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, so that it would be his salvation and the destruction of Pharaoh, whom Allah made a lesson for others.

Aaron: Moses' brother and companion in calling Pharaoh to believe in Allah, as he was eloquent and a speaker. Moses appointed him over his people when he went to meet Allah on Mount Tur. But the trial of Samiri occurred, leading the Israelites to worship a golden calf that lowed. Aaron called them back to worship Allah instead of the calf, but they grew arrogant. When Moses returned and saw what his people had come to, he reproached Aaron severely.

Jonah: a messenger sent to Nineveh's people, calling them to worship Allah alone, but they refused and grew arrogant. He left, threatening punishment after three nights; they feared for themselves and believed, so Allah removed the punishment. Jonah sailed in a ship; when they were about to drown, they cast lots to decide which man to throw overboard. It fell three times to Jonah, who threw himself into the sea. The fish swallowed him; Allah inspired it not to eat him. Jonah asked his Lord to release him from the darkness; Allah answered and sent him to a hundred thousand or more.
